business_problem: Fashion-design students at Istituto Secoli struggled to deepen their collection concepts because online research was shallow, algorithmically narrowed and slow to turn into reliable inspiration.
solution_summary: Istituto Secoli and IBM Client Engineering created a proof-of-value tool called CreativIA on IBM watsonx.ai, IBM watsonx.data and IBM Cloud Code Engine. The solution supports two parts of the concept-creation workflow. First, watsonx.ai takes a student's initial sentence and expands, rephrases and enriches it so the student can explore complementary directions instead of remaining stuck in an abstract starting point. Second, a search experience uses natural-language queries over a curated database of professor-selected articles and images stored in watsonx.data, helping students find semantically relevant references rather than generic internet results. Code Engine provides the runtime for the demo environment used in student testing. The resulting architecture combines creative ideation and governed reference retrieval in one tool, giving fashion students an AI-assisted way to research, refine and broaden collection concepts without replacing their own creative judgment.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Expands and enriches student concept prompts so designers can explore broader creative directions.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.data
solution_components.role: Stores the curated article and image corpus used by CreativIA's semantic search capability.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloud Code Engine
solution_components.role: Hosts the AI-powered tool and its demo environment for user testing and iterative improvement.

data_flow: Students enter an initial concept into watsonx.ai for expansion, then query a curated corpus in watsonx.data for relevant articles and images, and the resulting ideas and references are surfaced through the CreativIA application hosted on Code Engine.
business_outcome: CreativIA improved concept-development research for students, achieved strong adoption and satisfaction in testing, and gave Istituto Secoli a differentiated educational tool that strengthens its reputation for combining fashion training with technology.
metrics: 100% of all students involved in the testing acknowledged CreativIA as a valuable tool
65% of student research actively used the tool's core features
architecture_clues: The proof of value split the experience into concept expansion and semantic search over curated content.
The initial corpus came from a single integrated website during testing.
IBM Client Engineering ran user testing with students to refine features and UX.
